title: How many sides does the snowflake have at any step?
description: The video counts the sides of the snowflake of {{NAME_3}} at the first few steps by multiplying by four each time. It writes the pattern for Step n and checks it at Step two and Step three.
teaching_notes: One idea: every side becomes four sides, so the number of sides is multiplied by four at each step. Watch for students who add four sides at each step instead of multiplying.

video_script.why: The child counts the sides the way the example in the book does, and then writes the pattern for any step.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the number of sides by four at each step, and read the pattern for Step n.
video_script.anchor: the snowflake of {{NAME_3}} in the book, with a table of steps and the number of sides
video_script.payoff_line: At Step n the shape has three times four to the power n sides

final_answer.value: 3 x (4 to the power n) sides at Step n
final_answer.spoken: three times four to the power n sides at Step n

names.{{NAME_3}}: Swedish mathematician who described the snowflake in 1904

hold_back: Answer: 3 x (4 to the power n) sides at Step n
maths_rules: each side becomes 4 sides, so the count is multiplied by 4
Step n: 3 x 4 x ... x 4 (n times) = 3 x (4 to the power n)
video_script.design: A table of steps and sides grows one row at a time, with an arrow marked times four between rows; the rule for Step n is written at the bottom.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the snowflake at Steps 0, 1 and 2 in a row; a table with the heading sides

marks.book: the title card and the three frames appear
marks.ask: the table appears with a question mark in the row for Step n

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the snowflake of {{NAME_3}}.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The number of sides changes at every step. How many sides does the shape have at Step n?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board with the question mark underlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one side cut into 3 equal parts; a bump raised over the middle part; the 4 pieces of the new shape are numbered 1 to 4

marks.bump: a bump rises over the middle part of one side
marks.four: the four pieces are numbered one to four
marks.rule: the words each side becomes 4 sides are written

beats.removed: the middle part of the side
narration: <bookmark mark='bump'/>Raise a bump over the middle part of a side, as in the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The side is replaced by four pieces, two outer thirds and two sides of the bump.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 0 has 3 sides. Each step turns every side into 4 sides.

marks.given: the starting count and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Step zero has three sides, and each step turns every side into four sides.

beats.on_screen: To find: number of sides at Step n

marks.find: the words sides at Step n are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of sides at Step n.

marks.rule: the arrow times 4 appears between Step 0 and Step 1
marks.calc: 3 x 4 = 12 is written in the row for Step 1

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, multiply the sides by four, because each side becomes four sides.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>At Step one, three times four is twelve sides.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 12 x 4 = 48 sides. Step 3: 48 x 4 = 192 sides.

marks.two: 12 x 4 = 48 is written in the row for Step 2
marks.three: 48 x 4 = 192 is written in the row for Step 3

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, go on in the same way. At Step two, twelve times four is forty eight sides.
<bookmark mark='three'/>At Step three, forty eight times four is one hundred and ninety two sides.

beats.on_screen: Step n: 3 x 4 x 4 x ... (n fours) = 3 x (4 to the power n)

marks.list: the counts are rewritten as 3, 3 x 4, 3 x 4 x 4 and so on
marks.power: the Step n row is filled with 3 x (4 to the power n)

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step three, find the pattern. Each step multiplies the sides by four once more.
<bookmark mark='power'/>Step n has three multiplied by four, n times. That is three times four to the power n.

beats.on_screen: Check: n = 2: 3 x 16 = 48. n = 3: 3 x 64 = 192. Both match the table.

marks.two: 3 x 16 = 48 is written and ticked against the table
marks.three: 3 x 64 = 192 is written and ticked against the table

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step four, put the steps back in the rule. At Step two, four to the power two is sixteen. Three times sixteen is forty eight.
<bookmark mark='three'/>At Step three, four to the power three is sixty four. Three times sixty four is one hundred and ninety two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3 x (4 to the power n) sides at Step n
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>At Step n the shape has three times four to the power n sides.
